text: Καὶ βαπτισθέντων. Non simplex lotio, sed pietatis opus : juxta illud in fine Itinerarii Willebrandi ab Oldembourg, Symmictorum Allatianorum, 1 : Igitur et nos carnem interioris nostri hominis restitui et mundari sperantes, descendimus, et lavabamur in eodem Jordane. Idemque in nonnullis aliis Itinerariis.
anchorLine: σθέντων (n), μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐκοιμήθη ὁ ἀδελφὸς
en: On Καὶ βαπτισθέντων: this was not a simple washing but an act of piety, as in that passage at the end of the Itinerary of Willebrand of Oldenburg, in the Symmicta of Allatius, 1: 'So we too, hoping that the flesh of our inner man be restored and cleansed, went down and were washed in the same Jordan.' The same is found in several other Itineraries.

text: Τὸν φοῦρνον, et cap. 184, τὸν φουρνόν. Aliis est φοῦρνος. Vide Vitam Nili Junioris, p. 31 ; et Glossarium Meursii. A φοῦρνος fit φουρνητόριν seu φουρνητόριον, quod per furnum transiit, furno coctum et præparatum est ; in narratione de rebus Armeniæ, Auctar. Combefis. II, c. 281 B.
anchorLine: τὸν φοῦρνον (o) ὁ ἀδελφὸς Γεώργιος. Εἶτα μετὰ τὸ
en: On Τὸν φοῦρνον, and in ch. 184, τὸν φουρνόν. Elsewhere it is φοῦρνος. See the Life of Nilus the Younger, p. 31, and the Glossary of Meursius. From φοῦρνος comes φουρνητόριν or φουρνητόριον, that which has passed through the furnace, baked and prepared by the furnace; in the account of Armenian affairs, Combefis, Auctarium II, col. 281 B.

text: Τὸν ἐπικέρνην. Magis in usu est πιγκέρνης, pincerna, et πικέρνης. Interdum tamen reperitur ὁ ἐπικέρνης, quod est magis Græcum. Sic p. 181 Juris Græco-Romani ; et p. 522, post Excerpta C[…]ni.
anchorLine: ελεῖν. Καὶ δὴ πείθουσι τὸν ἐπιχέρνην (p) αὐτοῦ διὰ
en: On Τὸν ἐπικέρνην: the form πιγκέρνης (cupbearer, pincerna) is more usual, also πικέρνης. Occasionally, however, ὁ ἐπικέρνης is found, which is more properly Greek. So at p. 181 of the Jus Graeco-Romanum, and at p. 522, after the Excerpta of C[…].

text: Ἀπὸ ὀμμάτων. Una voce ἀπόμματος. De Christo Gregorius papa, epistola ad Germanum CP. act. 4 synodi 7 : Καὶ ἀπομμάτους ὠμμάτωσεν. Et cæcos illuminavit. Sic t. 1, hujus Sylloges, p. 570 B. Ἦν ἀπὸ δούλων· fuerat servus. Et in Vita Eupraxiæ, n. 20, Martii 13, ἣν ἔλεγον ἀπόδουλον εἶναι. Hoc est opinor, quam dicebant fuisse ancillam.
anchorLine: Ἰουλιανὸς, ἀπὸ ὀμμάτων (q). Οὗτος ὁ ἀββᾶς Ἰουλιανὸς
en: On Ἀπὸ ὀμμάτων: it is one word, ἀπόμματος. Of Christ, Pope Gregory in his letter to Germanus of Constantinople, act 4 of the Seventh Council: 'And he gave sight to the blind' (Καὶ ἀπομμάτους ὠμμάτωσεν). So in vol. 1 of this Sylloge, p. 570 B. Ἦν ἀπὸ δούλων: 'she had been a slave.' And in the Life of Euphraxia, n. 20, March 13, 'whom they said was a former slave' (ἣν ἔλεγον ἀπόδουλον εἶναι). This, I think, means: whom they said had been a maidservant.

text: Διέκρινε τὸ κοινωνῆσαι et κοινωνῆσαι διακρίνομαι. Hinc Diacrinomeni, hæretici, quorum mentio apud Leontium, De sectis, act. 4, 5, 6 et 7 ; Photium, cod. 24 ; Nicephorum, Hist. lib. xviii, cap. 45. Præcipue vero memoratur Joannes Diacrinomenus, cujus Historia ecclesiastica citatur act. 5 concilii generalis septimi. Ἰωάννης, inquit Theodorus Lector, lib. ii ὁ Διακρινόμενος μετὰ Σεβήρου ἱστορεῖ. Seu potius meo quidem judicio κατὰ Σεβήρου, adversus Severum, quamvis Nicephorus legisse se μετὰ ostendat, dum scribit, lib. xvi, cap. 29. Ἱστορεῖ δὲ Ἰωάννης ὁ αὐτῷ (Σεβήρῳ) διακρινόμενος. Quinetiam hujus Historiæ meminit Photius, Bibliothecæ cap. 41 ; sed quod conjicit esse Joannis presbyteri Ægeatæ, graviter errat : siquidem Joannes Ægeates vel Ægeota Nestorianus fuit, auctore ipso Photio, cod. 55 et Leontio act. 9 ; utque legitur in libello Precum ante epistolam Hormisdæ, 75 ; et in concilio generali 6, act. 11 et 15. Historicus autem Joannes Diacrinomenus, oppositæ prorsus hæreseos, necnon juxta Photium laudator conciliabuli Ephesini, Dioscori et sociorum. Denique in Demonstrationibus chronicis, quas exhibuit publico usui Franc. Combefisius, ὁ Διακρινόμενος est Joannes iste.
anchorLine: Ἱεροσολύμων, καὶ διέκρινε τὸ κοινωνῆσαι αὐτῷ (r). Ἐν
en: On Διέκρινε τὸ κοινωνῆσαι: κοινωνῆσαι and διακρίνομαι. Hence the Diacrinomeni, heretics, mentioned in Leontius, De sectis, acts 4, 5, 6 and 7; Photius, cod. 24; Nicephorus, Hist. bk 18, ch. 45. Chiefly remembered is John Diacrinomenus, whose Ecclesiastical History is cited in act 5 of the seventh general council. 'John,' says Theodore Lector, bk 2, 'the Diacrinomenus, writes with Severus' (μετὰ Σεβήρου). Or rather, in my judgment, κατὰ Σεβήρου, against Severus, although Nicephorus shows that he read μετά, when he writes, bk 16, ch. 29: 'John, who was at odds with him (Severus), writes.' Photius, Bibliotheca ch. 41, also mentions this History; but his conjecture that it is by John the priest of Aegae is a grave mistake, since John of Aegae (or Aegeota) was a Nestorian, on the authority of Photius himself, cod. 55, and of Leontius act 9, and as is read in the Libellus of Prayers before the letter of Hormisdas, 75, and in general council 6, acts 11 and 15. The historian John Diacrinomenus, by contrast, was of the directly opposite heresy and, according to Photius, a praiser of the conciliabulum of Ephesus, of Dioscorus and his partisans. Finally, in the Chronicle Demonstrations which Francis Combefis made public, ὁ Διακρινόμενος is this John.

text: Εἴ τις ἐὰν προσκομίσει. Interpres Ambrosius, Si quis inciderit. An legebat προσκόψει ? Cyrillus Alexandrinus apud Eustratium, quem luce donavit Allatius, p. 571, 572 : Τὰς ὑπέρ γε τῶν κεκοιμημένων ποιεῖσθαι λιτάς, προσκομίζειν τε, καὶ μεγάλα (f. μάλα) ἐμφρόνως οἱονεὶ παρόντι Χριστῷ διὰ τῆς ἁγίας καὶ μυστικῆς θυσίας.
anchorLine: ὅτι εἴ τις ἐὰν προσκομίσει (s) ἐν τῷ κοινοβίῳ ὑμῶν,
en: On Εἴ τις ἐὰν προσκομίσει: the translator Ambrosius has 'Si quis inciderit' (if anyone should fall in). Perhaps he read προσκόψει? Cyril of Alexandria, in Eustratius (whom Allatius brought to light), pp. 571-572: 'To make supplications for the departed, and to offer (προσκομίζειν), and very (read: most) wisely, as though Christ were present, through the holy and mystical sacrifice.'

text: Κρούσαι τὸ ξύλον. Apud Allatium, De confessione utriusque Ecclesiæ, c. 1560 : Κρούει τὸ κρούσμα ; c. 1569 : Κρούσμα ποιῆσαι. In vita S. Sabæ : Κρούσματος ὥρα. Et in Iambis Theodori Studitæ : Κρουσματοῦντος τοῦ ξύλου. Et : Σάλπιζε καιρῷ τὸ ξύλον. Et, ἐπειδὰν σαλπίσῃ τις τὸ ξύλον. Per metaphoram qua Dionysio pseudo-areopag. Οἱ ἀπερισάλπιγκτοι τῶν ἱερῶν τελετῶν : Quando ad collectam tuba insonuerit. In Regula sancti Pachomii, n. 2 ; Anastasius ad act. 4 synodi 7 : Orientales ligna pro campanis percutiunt.
anchorLine: ξύλον (t) τὸ νυκτερινὸν, ἀνακείμενος ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ κλι-
en: On Κρούσαι τὸ ξύλον ('to strike the wooden board'): in Allatius, De confessione utriusque Ecclesiae, col. 1560: 'he strikes the striking'; col. 1569: 'to make a striking.' In the Life of St Sabas: 'the hour of the striking.' And in the iambics of Theodore of Studium: 'when the board is being struck.' And: 'Sound the board in season.' And: 'whenever someone sounds the board.' By metaphor, as in Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite: 'those who have not been summoned by the trumpet of the sacred rites,' i.e. when the trumpet has sounded for the assembly. In the Rule of St Pachomius, n. 2; Anastasius at act 4 of the Seventh Council: 'Easterners strike wood in place of bells.'

text: Ἀβάλλαι. Cap. 49 et 78, ἀβάλε. Sic enim quoque solet efferri, atque etiam ἀββάλε. Estque notissima ex grammaticis dictio. Pseudo-Theophilus Alexandrinus, seu pseudo-Chrysostomus Savilii, t. VIII, c. 857, qui ex multis variarum bibliothecarum codicibus verus est · Christophorus Alexandrinus, sermone, Cui vita humana sit similis : Ἀβάλε τῇ ἀνθρωπότητι, ἀβάλε μοι ; Gregentius, f. 25 : Ἀβάλε ὅτι τὰς ἀσθενείας ὑμῶν ἐβάστασε · Theodorus Studita Laudatione in tertiam inventionem capitis sancti Joannis Baptistæ : Ἀβάλαι τοῦ ἀσελγεστάτου συμποσίου ! Proh impudicissimum convivium ! In sanctum Platonem, n. 27 : Vah ! ob ea quæ gesta tunc fuerunt. Apage facinora tunc temporis perpetrata ! Constantinus, De administratione imperii, paulo ante finem, p. 228 : Ἀβάλα λοιπὸν τῷ πιστεύοντι Χερσωνίτῃ πολίτῃ. Ubi Meursio est vox non intellecta. Sed aut legendum ἀβάλαι, aut ἀβάλαι per apocopen transiit in ἀβάλα, ut et in ἄβαλ apud Phavorinum et in Etymologico mayno. Epigrammate 70 Paradisi Joannis Geometræ, Ἀββάλε Μεζώης ! Atque eodem modo malim accipere in Metaphrasi Apollinaris, psal. lxviii, 8 : Ἀββάλε, πῶς τὸ πάροιθεν ἄναξ ἡγήσατο λαῶν ! quam cum interprete pro ἀνάβαλε, cunctare. Vid. Damascenum, De fidelibus defunctis, in fine.
anchorLine: Εἶπεν πάλιν· Ἀβάλαι (u), πόσα κλαύσομεν, καὶ
en: On Ἀβάλαι: in chapters 49 and 78, ἀβάλε. So too it is commonly pronounced, and also ἀββάλε. A very well-known word from the grammarians. Pseudo-Theophilus of Alexandria, or pseudo-Chrysostom in Savile, vol. 8, col. 857, who is true from many codices of various libraries; Christophorus of Alexandria, in the sermon 'To what is human life like?': 'Ἀβάλε to humanity, ἀβάλε to me'; Gregentius, fol. 25: 'Ἀβάλε, for he bore your weaknesses'; Theodore of Studium, in the Praise on the Third Finding of the Head of St John the Baptist: 'Ἀβάλαι of the most licentious banquet! Oh, shameless feast!' In 'On St Plato', n. 27: 'Ah! for the things done then. Away with the crimes then committed!' Constantine, De administratione imperii, a little before the end, p. 228: 'Ἀβάλα, then, to the believing Cherson citizen.' Where Meursius says it is a word not understood. But either ἀβάλαι must be read, or ἀβάλαι passed by apocope into ἀβάλα, as also into ἄβαλ in Phavorinus and in the Etymologicum Magnum. In epigram 70 of the Paradisus of John Geometres: 'Ἀββάλε Μεζώης!' I would prefer to take it likewise in the Metaphrasis of Apollinaris, Psalm 68 (LXVIII), 8: 'Ἀββάλε, how the leader formerly led the peoples!' which the interpreter renders as ἀνάβαλε, 'delay.' See Damascenus, On the faithful departed, at the end.

text: Λέγων. Josue v, 13, ad quem textum corruptus est pseudo-Chrysostomus, t. V editionis Etonensis, p. 997, l. XII : Ὁ τὴν μάχαιραν ἀσπασάμενος, καὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν τοῦ Ναυῆ συμπλέκεσθαι τοῖς πολέμοις προτρεπόμενος. Nam σπασάμενος, ostendunt verba sacra, καὶ ἡ ῥομφαία ἐσπασμένη ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ. Magis quoque prolarem, πολεμίοις. Qui gladium eraginavit, et Jesum filium Nave ad confligendum cum hostibus cohortatus est.
anchorLine: μὴ εἰσέλθῃ τις ξένος, λέγων (v)· Ἡμέτερος εἶ ἢ τῶν
en: On Λέγων: Joshua 5:13, to which text pseudo-Chrysostom has been corrupted, vol. 5 of the Eton edition, p. 997, line 12: 'He who drew the sword and urged Joshua son of Nave to join the wars.' For σπασάμενος, the sacred words show it: 'and the sword drawn in his hand.' I would rather put πολεμίοις. He who drew the sword and exhorted Jesus son of Nave to fight with the enemy.

text: Σαλός. Alias alia, et alii. Nunc nomen novum produco in lucem, e Niconis Pandecte ms. cujus λόγος λγʹ, continet in titulo : Καὶ ὅτι τοὺς τὸ σαλάτον κατὰ τὸν μέγαν Συμεὼν vel Συμεῶνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν ἐπιτηδεύοντας οἱ θεῖοι νόμοι ἀποδοκιμάζουσι· καὶ παντάπασιν ἄρτι τὰ τοιαῦτα κωλύουσιν.
anchorLine: καλής· ... ὡς σαλός (x). Λέγει μοι ὁ ἀββᾶς Σωφρόνιος·
en: On Σαλός: 'elsewhere another, and others.' I now bring a new name to light, from the manuscript Pandects of Nicon, whose discourse 33 contains this in its title: 'And that the divine laws reject those who practise the salatos [folly] after the manner of great Symeon or Symeon and Andrew, and now entirely forbid such things.'

text: Ἀδέλφιον ἐπίσκοπον Ἀραβήσσου. Vulgatius, Ἀραβ[?]σσ[?]ῦ. Et notitiæ Græcæ multum variant. De duobus Adelphiis Arabissi, vide Chrysostomi Vitas, cum Encycliis Leonis. Nam inter utrumque fuit Adolius, concilii Chalcedonensis tempore.
anchorLine: ὁ Ἀδέλφιον ἐπίσκοπον Ἀραβήσσου (y) εἶχεν δὲ καὶ ἀδελφὴν
en: On Ἀδέλφιον ἐπίσκοπον Ἀραβήσσου: the Vulgate (Latin) reading is Ἀραβ…σσ…; and the Greek notitiae vary a great deal. On the two Adelphii of Arabissus, see Chrysostom's Lives, with the Encyclia of Leo. For between the two there was Adolius, at the time of the Council of Chalcedon.
